tutorSurveys: The small group session went very well overall. During the lesson, Oliver experienced a brief moment of frustration after stepping away for the restroom and missing a portion of instruction. He became quiet and visibly upset in the corner of the table. The students and I gently checked in to see if he needed to visit the nurse or take a short walk. Oliver shared that he felt overwhelmed by missing the steps. I normalized his feelings, offered to review the specific problem step-by-step together, and asked if he would like to speak with Ms. Cassidy; he declined. After taking a few minutes to talk through the concept and reassure him, his mood improved and he finished the session in a positive state.

We did not complete Session 2 from the week of October 12. Anderson and Aria appeared content, participated, and completed the assigned work. Grey was eager to engage in conversation but reluctant to write, frequently offering reasons to delay or avoid the written tasks.

Today’s session took place in the 4A/B ELA classroom because the cafeteria was being used for the book fair. Scholars’ attention was frequently drawn to the wall displays, and the girls arrived late. Despite these distractions and the late arrivals, all scholars met today’s objective.

Scholars reviewed today’s Word of the Day and discussed its meaning and use. I also explained what morning dew is to support their background knowledge and understanding of the reading. Scholars then practiced breaking multisyllabic words into smaller parts. We compared robot and robin and discussed how an open or closed first syllable affects the vowel sound. Scholars practiced dividing and reading words connected to Thunder Cake, including thunder. We began reading the story using choral reading, and scholars read the selected portion back to me.

During today's session, the group demonstrated a high level of enthusiasm for learning. However, Jonah encountered significant difficulties with engagement and behavior throughout the lesson. Specifically, he struggled to remain in his assigned seat, engaged in arguments with his peers, and remained unfocused for the majority of the lesson. We lost a lot of learning time and were not able to get through most of the lesson today. Despite these challenges, Jonah showed great capability during the brief moments he did focus. When he actively participated and paid attention, he completed his work successfully and demonstrated understanding of the material. 

I have communicated these behavioral concerns to Mr. Sabani to ensure appropriate documentation and support a follow-up as needed.

The group demonstrated excellent behavior, engagement, and focus throughout the session, successfully grasping today’s core concepts. I would like to specifically highlight Kacper, who showed remarkable enthusiasm while working through the math exercises and performed exceptionally well.

During today’s session, Christopher successfully demonstrated improved focus and active participation after being seated separately from Jonah. Conversely, Jonah initially resisted the seating adjustment, remained easily distracted, and disrupted his peers; additionally, when given to opportunity to use the restroom he took his time which further reduced his available learning time. While the majority of the students were eager to learn and ready to participate, individual behavioral distractions and extended transitions ultimately reduced the overall instructional time for the group.
